route: explicit code labels in the deposit codebook + per-item mean match to the raw source file (route 1/9-style), corroborated by response-distribution semantics (route 8)
evidence: PDP_codebook.pdf keys every one of the 12 column codes to a distinct verbatim question, so the code->text tie is a label match, not an order inference. The one inferential link -- that the IRW item code is that same source column -- is pinned numerically: per-item means from PDP_data.csv vs live irw_fetch agree to <=4.7e-07 for all 12 (CB 3.325983/3.325983, S 2.466922/2.466922, SM 5.106424/5.106424, ...), while the smallest gap between any two item means is 0.010, i.e. 4 orders of magnitude larger, so no permutation of the 12 codes is consistent with the data. Content corroboration: the two personal-force dilemmas FB (2.70) and S (2.47) are the two lowest and SM (5.11, victim dies regardless) the highest. What this does NOT establish: the codebook's own code<->question assignment is taken as published -- notably VT=Vaccine and V=Vitamins, which reads backwards at a glance and cannot be separated statistically (means 4.78 vs 3.49 are both plausible either way). ORCHESTRATOR RE-CHECK (Step 5b, 2026-09-04): the agent's doubt about VT/V is resolved, not open. The two codes are content-coherent with the shipped text (VT = the vaccine-test dilemma, V = the vitamin-deficiency kidney dilemma), and the direction is predicted independently of the codebook: VT kills one to save millions, V forcibly takes a kidney from a man who survives to save six, so VT should be the more acceptable of the pair. Observed means are VT 4.780 vs V 3.493, in that order. Route 8 (semantic coherence) therefore separates the one pair the per-item mean identity check could not, and the codebook's assignment stands as published.

route: response format (route 2) + semantic coherence/block structure (route 8) + option-direction check against the study's faith item
evidence: Route 2 (response format) + route 8 (semantic coherence), on live server-side aggregates plus the OSF raw file that reproduces them (raw complete cases 2475 = live per-item n 2475 for all 7 items). (a) irw_table_sets: DSES_15 has 4 resp levels, all six other items have 6 -- the Czech DSES has exactly one 4-point item, its last ('In general, how close do you feel to God?'), so DSES_15 is pinned by format alone. (b) Direction: DSES_1 mean 1.10 among self-declared convinced atheists vs 3.15 among church members (DSES_15: 1.02 vs 2.17), so resp ascends with spiritual experience and the shipped anchors (1='Never or almost never', 1='Not close') are the right way round. (c) Correlation with the format-pinned DSES_15: DSES_1 .733 and DSES_14 .719 (the two items shipped with explicit-God wording) > DSES_11 .632 and DSES_10 .624 (religious vocabulary, no God referent) > DSES_12 .392 and DSES_13 .363 (no religious referent; these two correlate .677 with each other, the study's 'interpsychic' factor). (d) Off-by-one rejected: if the Czech version had dropped a later item, DSES_10 would be Underwood 10 'I feel God's love for me through others' and would have to sit with the .72-.73 pair; it is .624, the second lowest. NOT established: the order within {DSES_1, DSES_14}, within {DSES_10, DSES_11}, or within {DSES_12, DSES_13} -- these tests separate blocks, not items inside a block, which is why this is PARTIAL and not VERIFIED.
